name: define
title: Define
description: Define a product precisely, by a long interview that settles every decision one at a time, then write the documents that describe it.
notes:
## Define

Second skill of the Veebee chain (open source, MIT): from a blank page to a shipped product, one skill per step. Takes over from `eureka`.

**It defines, it never plans.** No question about how long the work takes, what gets built first, or what ships when.

- Interviews with `/grill-me`'s design tree and nothing else: no topic list, every question comes from something the user just said, so a game and a newsletter never get the same interview.
- Asks before going deep on a subject. A yes buys rounds of edge cases landing in `rules.md`; a no prunes the branch. The user decides where the product is precise and where it stays rough.
- Puts contradictions back in their face, both sides quoted, and never resolves one on its own. Each arbitration becomes a numbered file in `decisions/`.
- Sizes the product by **how many independent pieces it holds**, not how long it takes, then cuts it into milestones ordered by dependency. Each one is defined in turn with `/define <slug>`, inheriting everything the root settles.
- Every question card is answerable on its own: what is being settled, why it matters, what changes downstream, then the question. Options are two to five words and carry nothing else.
- Suggests, like `eureka`: almost every question carries a 💡 suggestion, the option the skill would pick and why, in one line, traceable to something the user said or a fact it found. Recommended option first with the reason as its description; a 💡 line in the chat.
- Shows the documents taking shape on a live page (Artifact tool), and ends every run on the project's milestone tree, read from disk.

Writes `CONTEXT.md` at the repository root for the vocabulary, and under `.veebee/`: `product.md`, `features.md`, `rules.md`, `journeys.md`, plus `decisions/` and `milestones/`.

Triggers: "définis mon produit", "fais-moi le cadrage", "on creuse mon idée", "cadre ce projet", "define this", "spec this out". Not for finding an idea from nothing: that is `eureka`.

No secrets, no environment variables. Source: https://github.com/The-Vibe-Company/veebee-skills

changes: From repository v0.10.0. The skill suggests, like eureka: almost every question carries a 💡 suggestion, the option it would pick and why, in one line, in the first person.
The reason is traceable: something the user said, a fact found and linked, or what the option commands downstream. Never what the skill knows about the user from elsewhere.
With the question tool the suggested option comes first with (Recommandé) on its label and the reason as its description; in the chat a 💡 line closes the options.
The opinion that used to close the question text lives in the suggestion, so the card carries the reasoning and the suggestion carries the pick.
No suggestion on the final check, on the offer to go deep, or on a question of taste.
From repository v0.9.0. The skill defines and no longer plans: no question about how long the work takes, what gets built first, or what ships when.
The size is asked as how many independent pieces the product holds. One piece, several pieces of one product, or several products.
Milestones are pieces ordered by dependency, stated as a reading order and not a schedule. The first one is the piece that carries the bet.
Every question card is answerable on its own: what is being settled, why it matters, what changes downstream, what bothers the skill, then the question naming its subject in full.

Options hold nothing but the option, two to five words. No justification inside them, no (Recommandé), no (exclusifs), no parenthesis on the question. The skill's opinion closes the question in the first person.
No calendar words anywhere: no soirées, no semaines, no livrer, no sprint.
The frontmatter description no longer breaks strict YAML parsers.
First Companion release, from repository v0.6.0, where the skill was renamed from crash-test to define and rewritten.
The design tree is the only engine: no topic list, no mandatory sections, every question traces back to an answer.
Going deep on a subject is asked, never assumed; the detail lands in rules.md.
Contradictions are put back immediately and written to decisions/.
No question limit, with a stop word and a ten-round checkpoint.
A folder of documents instead of one brief, and CONTEXT.md at the root so domain-modeling reads the same vocabulary.
Questions written the way you talk: one sentence, options that name the thing and stop, one reason line at most.
Every run ends on the project's milestone tree, read from disk, marking each one defined or to define.
